items.q: What defines a star as being on the 'main sequence'?
items.correct: It fuses hydrogen into helium in its core.
items.misconception: It is the largest stage of a star's life.
items.why: Students think main sequence = most spectacular. It's defined by the FUEL: hydrogen fusion. Stars spend most of their lives there because hydrogen is plentiful and fusion is stable.

items.q: What remnant forms after a very massive star's supernova if its core exceeds ~3 solar masses?
items.why: Correct answer: Black hole. “White dwarf” sounds right because it borrows the language of the topic — but it fails this question. Re-read the notes on why.

items.q: Why does iron stop fusion in a massive star's core?
items.misconception: Iron is too dense to compress
items.why: Correct answer: Iron fusion absorbs energy. “Iron is too dense to compress” sounds right because it borrows the language of the topic — but it fails this question. Re-read the notes on why.

items.q: What is the approximate Chandrasekhar limit, in solar masses?
items.why: The real figure is 1.4. The wrong options cluster deliberately close — anchor the exact number to one concrete fact so it can't drift.
